title: Autorepair blueprint catalog + simulated dry-run harness
creator: Marisol Ortega
description:
Summary: Build a curated catalog of autorepair blueprints (idempotent remediation snippets) that can be executed as discrete tasks by oncall and support tooling, plus a simulated dry-run harness that predicts outcomes and surface risks before any live run.

Goals: 1) Provide a discoverable, typed library of common remediation patterns (restart service, rotate keys, rollback config, scale instance group) with structured inputs and preconditions. 2) Implement a dry-run simulator that executes blueprints against a sandboxed state snapshot, returns deterministic diffs and estimated risk/confidence scores, and produces a machine-readable audit artifact. 3) Add safety gates: RBAC checks, rate limits, approval flows for high-risk blueprints, and automatic fallback to read-only diagnostics when run conditions are unmet. 4) Instrument telemetry for success rate, mean-time-to-repair (MTTR) delta, and false-positive rollback triggers.

Non-goals: full migration of legacy shelllets into blueprint DSL in this ticket; we'll create follow-ups for bulk migration and policy-onboarding.

Acceptance criteria:
- Catalog UI endpoint (internal console) lists at least 12 blueprint templates grouped by subsystem with typed input schema.
- Dry-run harness can ingest a workflow and return a simulated change-set plus confidence score within 10s for typical cases.
- Safety gate enforces approvals for blueprints flagged high-risk and logs approval records to audit stream.
- End-to-end test suite (unit + integration) covers simulation vs. small-scale live execution parity for 3 representative blueprints.
- Instrumented metrics published to ops telemetry dashboard and a sample alert for simulation/real mismatch is created.
comments: 2026-02-15 - Marisol: Created ticket to centralize autorepair blueprints and add a dry-run capability after incident INC-2026-02. Initial scope reviewed with SRE and Support.

2026-02-22 - Connor: Spike complete; validated prototype using a namespaced Kubernetes mock and an immutable transaction log. Simulation returns deterministic diffs but needs a confidence model. Added TODO to prototype a lightweight confidence heuristic. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-autorepair/pull/120

2026-02-28 - Design review (Aisha Reddy): UX for catalog and simulator results mocked. Recommend adding color-coded risk bands and a one-click promote-to-run flow guarded by an approval modal. Uploaded mock: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCExampleMock

2026-03-03 - PM (Samir Patel): Prioritized P1 due to repeated manual remediations causing <=30m MTTR spikes. Aligning with release opskit-2026.03; will coordinate canary with Dedicated customers via beta channel.

2026-03-07 - Connor: Implemented safety gating (RBAC + approval) and audit export. Discovered race condition when a dependent config update happens concurrently; added retry/backoff and a precondition check. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-autorepair/pull/142

2026-03-09 - QA (Lina Chow): Running integration smoke. Found simulation underestimates side-effect for 'scale-down-with-eviction' blueprint when eviction grace is >0. Added test to cover eviction windows and flagged as blocker for parity.
notes: Trade-offs considered: full TLA+ spec vs pragmatic example-based simulator. Chose pragmatic simulator with deterministic diffs and a confidence heuristic to deliver quickly; plan to iterate on formal verification in a later cycle. Also debating whether to embed cost estimation (API call counts, expected token usage) now or as follow-up — deferred to a separate ticket.
